title: What carbon monoxide does while you sleep 💤
subject: blood
description:
Does your home have a CO alarm? 👇

Carbon monoxide binds to your blood about 200 times more tightly than oxygen. Awake, it feels like flu. Asleep, the CDC says people can die before they feel anything.

Sources: CDC, "Carbon Monoxide Poisoning Basics" (2026); Mayo Clinic, "Carbon monoxide poisoning" (2025); StatPearls/NCBI, "Carbon Monoxide Toxicity" (2026).
tags: what carbon monoxide does to your body

scenes.text: Your blood grabs this gas 200 times harder than oxygen.
Carbon monoxide. No color, no smell. Furnaces, generators and car exhaust all make it.
It takes the spots on your red blood cells meant for oxygen.
Awake, you'd get a headache and dizziness. Mayo Clinic says it can feel like flu without the fever.
Asleep, you might feel nothing. The CDC says sleeping people can die before any symptoms.
More than 400 Americans die this way every year, and cases climb each winter.
